label: Epic of Gilgamesh
description: Early surviving epic concerned with kingship, friendship, mortality, flood memory, and the search for permanence.

label: Hebrew Bible / Old Testament
description: Composite scriptural library whose narrative, prophetic, wisdom, apocalyptic, and poetic forms became pervasive literary source material.

label: Iliad
description: Epic of war, rage, honor, mortality, and the costs of heroic culture.

label: Odyssey
description: Epic of return, identity, storytelling, hospitality, monsters, and homecoming.

label: Greek tragedy
description: Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides and the tragic tradition: fate, civic order, kinship, knowledge, and irreversible choice.

label: Plato — Republic
description: Political-philosophical dialogue on justice, education, social order, perception, and the ideal state.

label: Aristotle — Poetics
description: Early systematic analysis of tragedy, plot, imitation, recognition, reversal, and catharsis.

label: Mahabharata
description: Vast Sanskrit epic treating kinship, war, dharma, fate, ethics, devotion, and political order.

label: Ramayana
description: Sanskrit epic of exile, duty, kingship, loyalty, war, and ideal conduct, with extensive later adaptations.

label: Virgil — Aeneid
description: Roman national epic combining Homeric war and wandering with empire, duty, loss, and political destiny.

label: Ovid — Metamorphoses
description: Mythological poem organized around transformation; a major transmitter of Greco-Roman myth.

label: Beowulf
description: Heroic poem joining Germanic warrior culture, monsters, kingship, memory, and Christian retrospection.

label: One Thousand and One Nights
description: Layered frame-tale collection demonstrating recursive storytelling, wonder, travel, trickery, and survival through narrative.

label: The Tale of Genji
description: Court novel associated with Murasaki Shikibu; interiority, impermanence, desire, status, and memory.

label: Ferdowsi — Shahnameh
description: Persian epic history of kings, heroes, dynasties, conflict, and cultural memory.

label: Old Norse sagas & Eddic tradition
description: Saga and Eddic traditions of feud, fate, monsters, gods, heroic memory, and compressed prose narration.

label: Arthurian romance tradition
description: Evolving traditions around Arthur, quest, court, Grail, chivalric identity, betrayal, and the collapse of ideal orders.

label: Dante — Divine Comedy
description: Visionary journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise integrating theology, politics, autobiography, and classical inheritance.

label: Chaucer — Canterbury Tales
description: Frame narrative mixing estates satire, pilgrimage, competing genres, and storytelling voices.

label: Journey to the West
description: Comic-spiritual quest novel mixing Buddhist pilgrimage, folklore, monsters, satire, transformation, and episodic adventure.

label: William Shakespeare
description: Playwright whose tragedies, comedies, histories and poetic language became unusually dense sources for later literature.

label: Hamlet
description: Revenge tragedy centered on delay, performance, knowledge, grief, and unstable interpretation.

label: Cervantes — Don Quixote
description: Novel about a reader attempting to inhabit obsolete romance conventions; foundational for metafiction and the modern novel.

label: Milton — Paradise Lost
description: Biblical epic of rebellion, freedom, obedience, temptation, loss, and cosmic scale.

label: Swift — Gulliver’s Travels
description: Travel satire using invented societies to estrange politics, science, pride, reason, and human self-conception.
